concepts.label: node
concepts.gloss: A node is a forwarding domain represented as a vertex in the topology, within which traffic can be switched, adapted, terminated, or exposed for service access.
concepts.example: R1 is a node in the OTN-over-optical topology that hosts link termination points toward R2 and A1 and performs the OTU4/ODU2 adaptation.
concepts.evidence: Kind “node,” synonym “forwarding domain,” membership in t.topo, and instances R1–R3/A1–A3 indicate a topology-level forwarding entity; ruled out t.nrg, which is a switching rule set located on such an entity.

concepts.label: link-termination-point
concepts.gloss: A link-termination-point is a node-owned edge point at which one end of a topology link is attached and terminated.
concepts.example: nep-R1-R2 lies on R1 and terminates the R1 end of link-R1-R2, with a corresponding termination point on R2 at the other end.
concepts.evidence: Kind “termination,” synonyms “owned-node-edge-point” and “nep,” relations on-node and terminates t.link, and instances such as nep-R1-R2 identify a node-owned topology link endpoint; ruled out t.cep, which terminates a service realization rather than a topology link.

concepts.label: transitional-link
concepts.gloss: A transitional-link is an intra-node adaptation relation that carries traffic between different layer-protocol contexts according to a specified mapping or multiplexing qualifier.
concepts.example: At R1, the OTU4/ODU2 transitional-link maps an ODU2 client signal into an OTU4 server signal in accordance with the ODU2-into-OTU4 qualifier.
concepts.evidence: Kind “adaptation,” synonym “adaptation link,” relations at-node and adapts t.lpq, and instance “OTU4/ODU2 adaptation at R1” show an intra-node transition between protocol layers; ruled out t.link, which connects nodes rather than adapting layers inside one node.

concepts.label: service-interface-point
concepts.gloss: A service-interface-point is a node-associated access point through which a requester selects or reaches an offered connectivity service at a particular service or layer interface.
concepts.example: sip-A1-odu on A1 and sip-A3-odu on A3 are the two access points used to request the A1-to-A3 ODU2 connectivity service.
concepts.evidence: Kind “access,” relation on-node, reciprocal service relations accesses/uses with t.cs, and instances sip-A1-odu and sip-A3-odu indicate customer-facing service access points; ruled out t.ltp, which terminates topology links, and t.cep, which belongs to the internal service realization.

concepts.label: connectivity-service
concepts.gloss: A connectivity-service is a requested end-to-end connectivity construct between service interface points, with specified layer characteristics, whose realization is represented by connection endpoints over a topology.
concepts.example: cs-a1a3-odu2 provides ODU2 connectivity from sip-A1-odu to sip-A3-odu over the OTN-over-optical topology and is realized at the network side by CEPs at R1 and R3.
concepts.evidence: Kind “service,” relations uses t.sip, realized-by t.cep, and over t.topo, plus instance “cs-a1a3-odu2 (ODU2, A1 to A3),” identify an end-to-end connectivity intent; ruled out t.link, which is an individual topology adjacency rather than an offered service.

concepts.label: layer-protocol-qualifier
concepts.gloss: A layer-protocol-qualifier specifies the client/server layer and multiplexing or mapping treatment applicable to a connectivity service or its adaptation.
concepts.example: For the A1-to-A3 ODU2 service, the qualifier states that the ODU2 client is mapped into an OTU4 server container.
concepts.evidence: Kind “multiplex,” relation qualifies t.cs, and instance “ODU2 mapped into OTU4” identify a layer/mapping qualifier rather than a network resource; ruled out t.translink, which is the actual adaptation relation that applies this qualifier.

concepts.label: node-rule-group
concepts.gloss: A node-rule-group is a node-local collection of rules or capabilities that constrains which termination or connection points may be cross-connected within the node.
concepts.example: The R2 cross-connect rule group permits the appropriate ODU termination points on R2 to be joined so the A1-to-A3 service can transit from the R1-facing side toward R3.
concepts.evidence: Kind “switching,” relation on-node, and instance “R2 cross-connect rule group” indicate grouped node-local connectivity constraints; ruled out t.node, which is the forwarding domain governed by the rules, and t.cep, which is an endpoint rather than a switching policy.

concepts.label: link
concepts.gloss: A link is a topology-level adjacency between nodes whose ends are represented by link termination points owned by those nodes.
concepts.example: link-R1-R2 connects nodes R1 and R2 and is terminated at each end by the corresponding R1-facing and R2-facing node edge points.
concepts.evidence: Kind “link,” relation between t.node, inverse termination relations with t.ltp, and instances link-R1-R2 and link-A1-R1 identify topology adjacencies; ruled out t.translink, which represents same-node layer adaptation rather than inter-node adjacency.

concepts.label: topology
concepts.gloss: A topology is the graph-like network context that contains nodes and their links, potentially across multiple technology layers, and provides the resource domain over which connectivity services are realized.
concepts.example: The OTN-over-optical domain is a multi-layer topology containing nodes A1–A3 and R1–R3 together with links such as link-A1-R1 and link-R1-R2.
concepts.evidence: Kind “topology,” synonym “multi-layer topology,” contains relations to t.node and t.link, and instance “the OTN-over-optical domain” identify the enclosing network graph; ruled out t.cs, which runs over this graph but does not contain its resources.

concepts.label: connection-end-point
concepts.gloss: A connection-end-point is a service-specific endpoint on a node that marks where the network realization of a connectivity service begins, ends, or is bound into node connectivity.
concepts.example: cep-a1a3-R1 and cep-a1a3-R3 are the network-side endpoints on R1 and R3 belonging to the realization of cs-a1a3-odu2.
concepts.evidence: Kind “endpoint,” relations on-node and part-of t.cs, and instances cep-a1a3-R1 and cep-a1a3-R3 identify service-specific realization endpoints; ruled out t.sip, which is the exposed service access point, and t.ltp, which terminates a topology link.
